source.title: Next-Turn: Duration-Aware Streaming Endpoint Detection via Time-to-Next-Speech-Onset Prediction

source_direct_findings: Next-Turn predicts time-to-next-speech-onset as a duration-aware streaming endpoint-detection objective.
Its targets are derived from speech timestamps and require no additional endpoint annotation.
The paper reports a 25.9 percentage-point absolute endpoint-accuracy improvement within 320 ms over its strongest reported baseline.
The paper reports that joint training with the duration-aware objective complements binary endpoint detection and that gains increase with longer pauses.

frankenstein_inference.role: candidate complement/falsifier for DualTurn-style two-channel turn prediction, especially for distinguishing within-turn hesitation from actual endpoint
frankenstein_inference.why_high_value: It attacks the exact mid-utterance-pause failure mode that fixed silence timers create, while using a directly timestamp-derived target that is simpler to audit than semantic endpoint labels.
frankenstein_inference.non_equivalence: Next-Turn endpoint detection is not a replacement for DualTurn's full two-channel action/state vocabulary (EOT/HOLD/BOT/BC/VAD/FVAD). The two mechanisms should be compared and may be complementary.

required_discriminator.dataset: identical real German room-audio scenarios with mid-sentence hesitation, clause-final pause, backchannel, overlap and barge-in
metrics: false endpoint rate on within-turn pauses
median and p95 end-of-user-speech to decision latency
CPU/RAM/VRAM footprint inside whole-Frankenstein resident envelope
required_discriminator.promotion_rule: No production preference until German target-runtime evidence is observed and receipt-bound.
